quote: Theorem 1 Let X1, X2, ..., Xn be a set of dependent random variables sharing Archimedean copula having generator ψ1 such that Xi ∼ LS(λi, σi, F), i = 1, 2, ..., n. Let Y1, Y2, ..., Yn be another set of dependent random variables sharing Archimedean copula having generator ψ2 such that Yi ∼ LS(λi, ξi, G), i = 1, 2, ..., n. Assume that σ, ξ and λ ∈ D+ (or E+). Further suppose that φ2 ◦ ψ1 is super-additive, ψ1 or ψ2 is log-concave and X ≤st Y. If either rX(u) or rY(u) is decreasing in u, then σ−1 ≼w ξ−1 implies X1:n ≤st Y1:n.
model: series systems with dependent components sharing Archimedean copulas
family: location-scale LS(λ, σ, F) with common locations; generators ψ1, ψ2
compared: minima under weak majorization of reciprocal scale vectors and copula ordering

quote: Theorem 6 Let X1, X2, ..., Xn be independent with Xi ∼ LS(λi, σi, F) and Yi ∼ LS(λi, ξi, G). Suppose that σ, ξ, λ ∈ D+ (or E+). Then, if X ≤hr Y and i) either urX(u) or urY(u) is concave in u, then σ ≼m ξ ⇒ X1:n ≤hr Y1:n; ii) either urX(u) or urY(u) is increasing (decreasing) and concave in u, then σ ≼w (≽w) ξ ⇒ X1:n ≤hr Y1:n; iii) either urX(u) or urY(u) is increasing in u, and u·d/du(urX(u)) or u·d/du(urY(u)) is decreasing in u, then σ ≼p ξ ⇒ X1:n ≤hr Y1:n; iv) either urX(u) or urY(u) is increasing in u, and u²·d/du(rX(u)) or u²·d/du(rY(u)) is decreasing in u, then σ ≼rm ξ ⇒ X1:n ≤hr Y1:n.

quote: Theorem 7 Let X1, X2, ..., Xn be independent with Xi ∼ LS(λi, σi, F) and Yi ∼ LS(λi, ξi, G). Suppose σ, ξ, λ ∈ D+ (or E+). quote: Theorem 9 Let {X1,...,Xn} and {Y1,...,Yn} be two sets of independent random variables each following the multiple outlier LS model such that Xi ∼ LS(λ1, σ1, F), Yi ∼ LS(λ1, ξ1, F) for i = 1,...,n1 and Xi ∼ LS(λ2, σ2, F), Yi ∼ LS(λ2, ξ2, F) for i = n1+1,...,n. Suppose that (λ1,λ2), (σ1,σ2), (ξ1,ξ2) ∈ D+ (or E+). Now if urX(u) is decreasing in u and rX(u) is log-concave and 2-log-convex in u, then (1/σ1·n1, 1/σ2·n2) ≼m (1/ξ1·n1, 1/ξ2·n2) ⇒ X1:n ≥R−hr Y1:n.
